title: Clopen pieces and their affine lines are separated of finite type
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $U\subseteq Y$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] whose underlying subset is also closed in $|Y|$. Then $U$, with the restricted structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, is separated and of finite type over $k$. For every $r\in\mathbf N$, the relative affine space $\mathbf A^r_U$ of [def-sbc-affine-space], with its composite structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$, is also separated and of finite type over $k$. The empty open subscheme and $r=0$ are allowed.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $f:Y\to S$, and $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$. For every affine open $V\subseteq Y$, the inverse image $j^{-1}(V)$ is identified with $U\cap V$, with its subspace topology, by [def-weil-open-immersion]. Because $U$ is closed in $Y$, $U\cap V$ is closed in $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $V$ is quasi-compact; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-in-quasi-compact] therefore makes $j^{-1}(V)$ quasi-compact. This holds for every affine $V$, which is exactly quasi-compactness of $j$ in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 005C (lemma-closed-in-quasi-compact), applied on each affine open of Y; affine quasi-compactness: Algebra Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact)

proof.text: The open immersion $j$ is quasi-compact by Step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] gives that $j$ is of finite type. The given $f$ is of finite type, hence [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) applied to $j$ and $f$ shows that $f\circ j:U\to S$ is of finite type.

The diagonal $\Delta_{U/S}:U\to U\times_SU$ is the base change of $\Delta_{Y/S}:Y\to Y\times_SY$ along $j\times_Sj$. Indeed, a map into that pullback is a pair $u_1,u_2:T\to U$ with a common image in $Y$; equality $ju_1=ju_2$ forces $u_1=u_2$, since the open immersion $j$ [def-weil-open-immersion] is a monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism]. The pullback is therefore $U$, compatibly with both projections, by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The given separatedness of $f$ makes $\Delta_{Y/S}$ a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] to obtain a closed immersion $\Delta_{U/S}$; the same definition gives separatedness of $U\to S$.

source.place: Tag 01KK (definition-separated); diagonal base-change argument as in Tag 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence); closed-immersion base change: Morphisms Tag 01QR

proof.text: Fix $r\in\mathbf N$, put $X=\mathbf A^r_U$, and write $p:X\to U$. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $U$, [def-sbc-affine-space] identifies $p^{-1}(V)\to V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R[t_1,\ldots,t_r])\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Thus $p$ is affine by [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. The polynomial algebra is generated over $R$ by $t_1,\ldots,t_r$: every polynomial is a finite sum of coefficient multiples of products of these variables. These single affine charts cover each inverse image, so [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives that $p$ is locally of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), $p$ is quasi-compact and separated. Combining quasi-compactness with local finite type gives that $p$ is of finite type.

For separatedness of the composite $X\xrightarrow{p}U\to S$, factor its diagonal as $X\xrightarrow{\Delta_{X/U}}X\times_UX\xrightarrow{q}X\times_SX$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], the square with arrows $q$, $X\times_UX\to U$, $p\times_Sp:X\times_SX\to U\times_SU$, and $\Delta_{U/S}$ is cartesian: its data are two maps to $X$ whose images in $U$ coincide. Step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] make $q$ a closed immersion. Step 4 and [def-weil-proper-morphism] make $\Delta_{X/U}$ a closed immersion. Their composite is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-products], so $X\to S$ is separated by the definition.

source.place: Tag 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), proof of (1): factor the composite diagonal; closed immersions: Morphisms Tags 01QR and 01QS

proof.text: Both $p:X\to U$ and $U\to S$ are of finite type by Steps 4 and 2. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) to conclude that $X\to S$ is of finite type. Together with Step 5 this proves the second assertion for every $r$. When $U=\varnothing$, all inverse-image affine covers in the preceding checks are empty and the conclusions hold vacuously. When $r=0$, [def-sbc-affine-space] identifies $p$ with $\operatorname{id}_U$, recovering Steps 2 and 3. No nonemptiness or positive-rank hypothesis was used.

The statement is true on Spec k ⊔ Spec k, U=Y, U=∅, r=0/1/arbitrary and nonreduced Y, with no weakening against the parent. Every cited node is a Mathlib leaf or slopmaster2-closed, so no tool_uses are needed; no SGA source is used. There are no new nodes. A DAG-wide search found no duplicate of the combined statement.
